Following a hearing on the above-referenced motions conducted on April 28, 2011, and after due consideration, the Defendants' Motion to Dismiss is DENIED.



The Defendants' Motion to Dismiss is unsupported by affidavits or other evidence to rebut Plaintiffs' presumed status as aggrieved parties under  10A of the Boston Zoning Enabling Act, or to contradict Plaintiffs' standing under G.L. c. 240,  14A. Accordingly, accepting as true the allegations set forth in Plaintiffs' First Amended Complaint and drawing inferences therefrom in the Plaintiffs' favor, as it must, the court concludes that it is premature to dismiss the Plaintiffs' claims for lack of standing at this stage of the proceedings. The Motion is denied without prejudice to the Defendants renewing their standing challenges on a proper evidentiary basis.

The parties& cross motions for summary judgment in Case No. 09 Misc. 416827 were DENIED since there are genuine issues of material facts in dispute, with the following exception. On the undisputed facts, there was a procedural flaw in the Board proceeding at which the decision was made.  The hearing was called by the Board for the purpose of re-visiting the constructive grant to South Brockton LLC.  South Brockton was present at the hearing and prepared to present testimony from its representatives and experts on the merits of that issue.  The board never called for such testimony or any presentation whatsoever, either from South Brockton or anyone else.  Instead, without prior notice that it would do so, the Board confined itself to the evidence and presentations from its earlier proceeding.   A remand to the Board at which South Brockton and other interested parties are permitted to make such presentations is thus required. The plaintiff has requested that such a remand be deferred, however, pending resolution of the &zoning freeze& issue in Case No. 10 Misc. 442231 which may make such a remand unnecessary.  A status conference is scheduled for November 7, 2011 at 10:30 am in both cases to discuss this and other matters and determine how both cases should proceed from this point forward.  SO ORDERED. Findings: The above captioned case was tried by two highly profesional, competent and prepared counsel.  The case was heard and decided by a jury that in the Court's view was attentive to and engaged in the trial..
The factual basis of the case was a somewhat unique automobile accident (a car bursting through the front of Ms. Pearson's home).  The jury found for the plaintiff but awarded a sum that was just shy of the medical bills proferred to them through trial exhibits.   A motion for a new trial presents to a judge a limited role of review because the judge ruling on the motion should not decide the case as if he or she was acting as the fact finder; rather the judge should only set aside the verdict if satisfied that the jury failed to reach it's verdict by exercising an honest and reasonable judgment in accordance with the law.  Moose v. Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 43 Mass App. Ct. 420 (1992).  The Court does not feel comfortable putting itself into the jurors shoes when it does not appear the jury failed to act pursuant to it oath.  The Motion is denied.  So Ordered.  (Payne, Hon. John M. Jr.) Presiding Justice.

Based upon that finding, the plaintiff presented facts to successfully demonstrate an entitlement to relief.  Iannachchino v. Ford Motor Co. 451 Mass 623 (2008).  The difference between the verdict and the offer may not be great in terms of actual dollars, however it does represent an almost 2/3 increase.  As such a dismissal of the G.L. c.93A portion of this claim would not be appropriate. The Motion to Dismiss is Denied.  The parties may schedule the matter for further proceedings. Notice of Docket Entry. Hearing held on plaintiff Capital Trust Investments LLC&s motion for preliminary injunction.  The case concerns a mortgage plaintiff Capital Trust obtained by assignment, which it alleges encumbers the property at 1277 Massachusetts Avenue in Dorchester.  It further alleges that that mortgage is senior to a mortgage allegedly held by defendant Deutsche Bank on the same property.  Deutsche Bank has conducted a foreclosure sale of the property (the latest in a series that began almost a year ago, all previous of which had been re-noticed because of defects in the notice) and Capital Trust alleged that a transfer of the property pursuant to that sale was imminent.   The injunction sought was to prevent the transfer, sale or further encumbrance of the property until such time as the validity and priority of the Capital Trust mortgage is adjudicated.  A critical fact, which Capital Trust had not previously brought to the court&s attention, was disclosed by Deutsche Bank at the hearing.  The Capital Trust mortgage, on its face, does not encumber the property because the mortgagor did not sign it, only the mortgagee.  The mortgage may have been mistakenly drafted (the mortgagor may have been intended as the mortgagee and vice versa) but it would require reformation to &correct& that mistake and Capital Trust&s complaint neither disclosed that issue nor sought reformation.  A second critical fact was also disclosed.  According to Deutsche Bank, it was not the holder of the mortgage at the time it noticed and conducted the latest foreclosure sale.  Thus, a new sale must be noticed and conducted.  This will take several weeks.  Deutsche Bank represented at the hearing that no transfer (other than to defendant Deutsche Bank) will take place at least until such time as that new sale takes place.  Accordingly, Capital Trust&s motion for preliminary injunction was DENIED.  First, Capital Bank has not, as yet, shown a likelihood of success on the merits.  Such success would require both clear and convincing proof that its mortgage was mistakenly drafted and reformation of that mortgage, with nunc pro tunc effect.  Second, it has not shown an immediate and irreparable injury since its mortgage, whatever its validity and effect is ultimately determined to be, is &of record,& Capital Trust&s claims regarding it will be disclosed at any foreclosure sale since they would certainly be material to any prospective purchaser, and because a transfer of the property will not occur, at the earliest, until a new foreclosure sale takes place many weeks in the future.  With the goal of determining the merits of Capital Trust&s claims prior to that sale, an evidentiary hearing on those claims has been scheduled for February 3, 2011 at 2:00 p.m.  The issues to be tried include (1) whether the mortgage was mistakenly drafted and should now be reformed (an issue that likely will require testimony from the parties to that mortgage), (2) Capital Trust&s knowledge of the issues involved with that mortgage at the time of its acquisition, and the terms and conditions of that acquisition, including the amount of consideration paid, (3) Deutsche Bank&s knowledge of the (now) Capital Trust mortgage at the time Deutsche Bank acquired its interest and the reasonableness of its reliance (if any) on the invalidity of that mortgage, and (4) if the Capital Trust mortgage is reformed, whether that reformation should be nunc pro tunc in light of the above and other relevant factors, or whether other (and, if so, what) relief should be granted.  By no later than January 28, 2011, the parties must serve each other and file with the court (1) a list of all witnesses they intend to call at the evidentiary hearing, along with a short description of each witness& expected testimony, and (2) a list and copy of all exhibits they intend to offer into evidence.  Capital Trust voluntarily dismissed its claims against Doonan Graves & Longoria LLC and those claims are therefore DISMISSED in their entirety.&  (Long, J.)

STIPULATION OF THE PARTIES AS TO DOCKET ENTRIES AND REFILING 1. Parties acknowledge that certain docket entries pertaining to motions filed through the months of July and August 2011 in the above referenced matter have been mis-communicated to the court due to U.S. Postal service delivery problems to the Offices of counsel for the defendant. More than five separate envelopes from the Plaintiff's law firm and the Court, addressed to the Defendant's law office in Andover, Massachusetts, containing these motions were returned and marked undeliverable. 2. In particular a motion to strike the answer and counterclaim was filed by the Plaintiff on or about July 29, 2011. The Defendants never received the Motion, had no knowledge of these Motion and as such, no oppositions were filed by the Defendant. The Motion was allowed by the Court due to the lack of an opposition on August 3, 2011. 3. To preserve the docket and preserve all legal and procedural rights of all parties, the parties hereby stipulate as follows: A. The Motion to Dismiss and Opposition to the Motion to Dismiss as well as Supplemental filings made by both counsel after oral argument on or about September 19 and 20th, for purposes of the docket, are hereby deemed received by the court and taken under advisement by the court. The parties have presented all issues relative to the Defendant's motion to Dismiss and Plaintiffs opposition for the court's consideration. B. The Plaintiff will re-file its motion to strike the Defendant's Answer and Counterclaim pursuant to Superior Court Rule 9A and fax, email and by US Mail the Motion to Defendant's counsel for him to provide his opposition in a timely manner consistent with the Rule 9A. C. Defendant withdraws his motions for Reconsideration. D. Parties withdraw all motions or requests for any sanctions directed to any party, the court and/or the clerk's office as the underlying discrepancy were entirely due to lack of adequate mail delivery. E. Parties agree that no further motions shall be filed with the court other than by the Rule 9A and 9D procedure and that any further filings coming directly to the clerks' office not in compliance will be returned to counsel. F. Parties agree to use their telephone equipment, e-mails and fox machines to communicate in the future, to assure that all involved receive their notices.

The following event: Pre-Trial Conference scheduled for 07/08/2015 11:00 AM has been resulted as follows: 
Result: Pretrial conference held. Attorney Henry Lane appeared for Plaintiff. Defendant Howard Fease, pro se, participated via telephone.  The court reviewed the parties' PTC memo.  As result of the discussion, it was decided:  Byron Andrews will be Plaintiffs' expert and, to the extent Defendant wants to inquire of him, it will be done on cross-examination.  Attorney Lane will provide Mr. Andrews' sketch plan to Defendant for his review by September 4, 2015, together with any plans and sketches referenced thereon.  Defendant withdrew witnesses Nydam, Vandenakker, and Dzicek from his witness list and they will not be called at trial unless Defendant informs the court and Plaintiffs' counsel by the end of the day July 10, 2015, of his intention to do so.  If he so decides, Plaintiffs will have the right to notice their depositions.  Defendant also withdrew Barbara Kinney, keeper of the records of the Conservation Commission, from the witness list.  Defendant agreed to present his title expert's direct testimony by affidavit, which shall be filed with the court and served on Plaintiffs' counsel with all exhibits attached, by September 4, 2015.  Defendant will present his written direct testimony by affidavit since he is self-represented, rather than as a narrative at trial.  That affidavit shall be served and filed by September 4, 2015.  A tentative trial date has been set, but it will not be confirmed by the court until discovery is concluded and the dates set forth herein have been met by the parties.  Whether the court will take a view is left to the court's decision, after trial.  The parties have agreed to work on the Agreed Statement of Facts to see if they can reach further consensus.  They did agree that all instruments and plans recorded with the Worcester Registry of Deeds are admissible, without certification.  

(Notice of docket entry sent to Atty. Henry Lane and to Pro Se Howard Fease)
